hints: A complete moment definition needs both the force and the perpendicular separation from the stated point.
walkthrough: Use the point named in the question as the reference point.
The moment is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from that point to the force's line of action.

ai_rubric.observable: States that moment equals force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the force's line of action.

hints: Take moments about Q so that the unknown ground force R has no moment.
The tree's weight is 270g and its perpendicular distance from Q is 1.2 m.
The post force is perpendicular to PQ. Use the geometry to express PQ as 1.6 / cos θ before balancing the two moments.
walkthrough: Take moments about Q. The ground force R acts through Q, so it contributes zero moment.
The tree's weight is W = mg = 270 × 9.81 N and its horizontal perpendicular distance from Q is 1.2 m, giving a moment of 1.2 × 270 × 9.81 N m.
The post force F is perpendicular to PQ, so its moment arm is PQ. Since the horizontal separation QP is 1.6 m, PQ cos θ = 1.6 m and PQ = 1.6 / cos θ.
Solving gives cos θ = 2880 / 3179... = 0.906, so θ = 25°.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms the weight moment about Q as 1.2 × 270 × 9.81.
Uses the post-force moment as 1800 × (1.6 / cos θ).
Equates the moments and obtains θ = 25° from a valid rearrangement.

hints: The three forces on an object in equilibrium must add to zero, so use the end of each vector as the start of the next.
Keep the given weight vector unchanged, then add the post force and ground force at their specified directions so the triangle closes.
walkthrough: For equilibrium, the vector sum of the post force F, ground force R and weight is zero, so the three vectors must form a closed tip-to-tail triangle.
Retain the given downward weight vector at its supplied scale.
Draw and label F at 25° from vertical on the anticlockwise side, using the 1800 N scale length.
Draw and label R as the closing vector at 37° from vertical on the clockwise side; its tip must meet the starting point of the given weight vector.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a closed tip-to-tail triangle including the supplied weight vector.
Labels F at 25° ± 3° anticlockwise from vertical and R at 37° ± 3° clockwise from vertical, with F drawn to the 1800 N scale.

hints: The force on the post has magnitude 1800 N and acts normally on its top surface.
Rearrange p = F / A to A = F / p, and convert 150 kPa to pascals before substituting.
walkthrough: The contact force is the 1800 N post force, and the pressure is 150 kPa = 150 × 10³ Pa.
From p = F / A, rearrange to A = F / p.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges p = F / A to use A = 1800 / (150 × 10³).
Obtains a contact area of 0.012 m².
